podcasts.name: No Priors
podcasts.title: The New Apex Predator: CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz on Adversaries Armed With AI Agents
podcasts.description: Adversaries are already running AI agents, and the fastest attacks now play out in seconds. Sarah Guo and Elad Gil sit down with CrowdStrike president and CEO George Kurtz on what AI-equipped attackers mean for enterprise security. George explains how agents are flattening the adversary pyramid by putting advanced tradecraft in the hands of low-skill attackers, and why CrowdStrike and Nvidia are building a frontier-style lab of their own to train security models. They also get into how open-weight and closed models compare on security, where CrowdStrike is directing its platform investment, lessons from the recent Hugging Face incident, and why George sees AI, like every platform shift before it, as a net creator of opportunity. Sign up for new podcasts every week. podcasts.name: The MAD Podcast with Matt Turck
podcasts.title: State of AI 2026: The Biggest Stories of the Year (and AGI in 2027?) | Nathan Benaich
podcasts.description: AGI in 2027. That’s the last line of this year’s State of AI Report, and its author Nathan Benaich (Air Street Capital) is back for the third year to defend it. AI is now building AI: Claude leads 26% of Anthropic’s own model R&D, up from under 1% in February, but Nathan thinks “research taste” is the wall. OpenAI’s evaluation agents ended up inside Hugging Face’s systems, only a Chinese open-weight model could help investigate, and Nathan now argues cyber risk matters more than existential risk. Catching up to OpenAI or Anthropic from scratch costs about a trillion dollars, which is why “you either die trying to get to the frontier, or live long enough to serve inference.” Americans would rather live next to a nuclear plant than a data center, $50B of projects are stalled, and all 27 EU countries together have fewer GPUs than one top US cluster. Sovereign AI is “like a national airline: it’s still someone else’s airplane.” Also: the three-lab race and the fate of the neo labs, models vs. harnesses, why he won’t give a personal AI agent his credit card, the Codex adoption gap and why OpenAI should open a store, enterprises owning their own AI instead of renting it, and the morning a solo GP woke up to twelve expert interviews his agent ran overnight. podcasts.name: AI & I by Every
podcasts.title: How a Frontier Team Can Help Your Company Keep Up With AI
podcasts.description: Check out Gemini Audio: https://goo.gle/Every-Gemini-Audio Every time a new AI model drops, companies face the same dilemma: Figure out what’s new and how to use it, or focus on getting work done. Every solves this dilemma with a frontier team: a small group that tests new models and turns useful experiments into tools and workflows for the rest of the company. On this week’s episode of The Every Podcast , Natalia Quintero sits down with all seven members of Every’s frontier team to ask what they’re building—from a tabless browser that helps protect your attention to a personal agent orchestrator called Minga—and what they want to try next.
